name: chmod
plain: `chmod` changes who may read, write or execute a file. Every file has three sets of permissions: for its owner, for its group and for everyone else.
It is how you make a script executable, lock down a private key, and, in security work, how you spot dangerous settings such as world-writable files or the SUID bit.
when: Make a script runnable: chmod +x script.sh.
Protect a secret: chmod 600 private.key (ssh refuses keys that others can read).

examples.title: Make a file executable  (+x)
examples.explain: +x adds the execute permission for everybody who already has some access. Without it ./run.sh fails with 'Permission denied'.

examples.title: Numeric modes  (644, 600, 755, 700)
examples.explain: Each digit is owner, group, others. Read = 4, write = 2, execute = 1, added together: 6 = read+write, 7 = all, 5 = read+execute, 0 = nothing. 600 means only the owner can read and write; 755 is a typical program; 644 a normal file.

examples.title: Symbolic modes  (u g o a, + - =)
examples.explain: u = owner (user), g = group, o = others, a = all. + adds, - removes, = sets exactly. This line adds execute for the owner, removes write from the group and removes everything from others.

examples.title: Recursive  (-R)
examples.explain: Applies to the folder and everything inside it. Be careful with -R on a whole system folder.

examples.title: Copy permissions from another file  (--reference)
examples.explain: Gives other.sh exactly the permissions of run.sh.

examples.title: See what changed  (-v, -c)
examples.explain: -v reports every file processed; -c reports only files whose mode actually changed.

examples.title: Special bits: SUID, SGID, sticky
examples.cmd: chmod u+s prog;  chmod g+s dir;  chmod +t /tmp/shared
examples.explain: SUID (4000) runs a program with its owner's privileges, which is why find / -perm -4000 is a privilege-escalation check. SGID (2000) and the sticky bit (1000, as on /tmp) control group inheritance and who may delete files.

options.plain: The new permissions: a number such as 755, or a symbolic form such as u+rwx,go-w.
Like verbose, but report only when a change is made.
Report every file that is processed.
Use the mode of RFILE instead of giving a mode.

options.use: Protection against a disastrous chmod -R on /.

mistakes: chmod 777 is almost never the answer: it lets everybody change the file.
chmod -R 777 or chmod -R +x on a tree makes data files executable.
ssh refuses private keys that other users can read: use 600 (and 700 for ~/.ssh).
Directories need the execute bit to be entered: a folder with r but no x lists names but cannot be opened.
try: Create a file, set each of 000, 400, 600, 644, 755 and try to read, write and run it.
Find files in /usr/bin with the SUID bit using find / -perm -4000 2>/dev/null.
Make a script executable and run it, then remove the bit and see the error.
see_also: chown(1), chgrp(1), umask(1), ls(1) -l, find(1) -perm, stat(1), getfacl(1), setfacl(1).
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
